Name: Netflix
End_target_text: The 2022 ‘net zero’ claim refers to a temporary balance via credits, while long-term decarbonization efforts continue.
Interim_target_text:
“Reduce absolute GHG emissions 46% by 2030 from a 2019 baseline, across Scopes 1, and 2.
(Netflix Environmental Social Governance Report 2024, pg. 7)

For Scope 3: Reduce 55% per USD of value added by 2030, aligning with the global halving of emissions required to reach net zero by 2050.”
(Netflix Environmental Social Governance Report 2024, pg. 13)
Targets_notes:
"We continue to make progress against the targets we set in March 2021 to: 1) Reduce our emissions by roughly half by 2030, and 2) Match our remaining emissions from 2022 onwards in support of global net zero goals, through investments in verified natural climate solutions and super pollutant (e.g., methane) destruction. Beyond 2030, Netflix will continue to reduce our emissions in line with the latest climate science until global net zero is achieved" (Netflix Environmental Social Governance Report 2023, pg. 10).

Netflix has also set an Absolute Emissions Reduction Target by 2030: "Target: 46% by 2030 Absolute Reduction (reduce absolute emissions by 46% from a 2019 baseline)" (Netflix Environmental Social Governance Report 2023, pg. 11: https://s22.q4cdn.com/959853165/files/doc_downloads/2024/6/2023-Netflix-Environmental-Social-Governance-Report.pdf

Scope 3 goal: "To contribute to the global halving of emissions by 2030, which scientists prescribe as an interim step to reach global net zero in 2050, we have committed to reduce our Scope 3 emissions 55% per $USD of value added by 2030" (Netflix Environmental Social Governance Report 2023, pg. 25).
“Netflix’s near-term science-based target has been validated by SBTi under the 1.5°C pathway. 

The 2022 ‘net zero’ claim refers to a temporary balance via credits, while long-term decarbonization efforts continue. Annual emissions are verified by EY with limited assurance covering all scopes.”
Coverage_notes:
Gases covered: "The majority of the reported CO2e emissions are from CO2 with the remainder being composed of CH4, N2O, and hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), noting that perfluorocarbons (PFCs), SF6, and NF3 are not applicable to Netflix’s emissions. GHG Emissions – Scope 1 includes natural gas, jet fuel, gasoline, diesel, fugitive emissions from refrigerant leakage, and biogenic emissions for CH4 and N2O" (EY Independent Accountants' Review Report 2023, pg. 3: https://web.archive.org/web/20250918141502/https://s22.q4cdn.com/959853165/files/doc_downloads/2024/6/NFLX-FY23-independent-Accountants-Report.pdf).

All scopes covered in target & greenhouse gas inventory: Netflix Environmental Social Governance Report 2023, pg. 12-18, pg. 79: https://s22.q4cdn.com/959853165/files/doc_downloads/2024/6/2023-Netflix-Environmental-Social-Governance-Report.pdf
“Netflix’s GHG inventory follows the GHG Protocol and covers Scopes 1, 2, and 3, including upstream and downstream emissions. The company publicly discloses emissions and third-party assurance reports annually.”
Published_plan_measures: Measures for all emission scopes that are covered by the target, Information on the emission reductions expected from these measures within a certain time period, Schedule for regular review of measures, Information on the extent to which measures will be applied (e.g. if switching to EVs, what share of the fleet; if installing an own solar PV installation, what is the installed capacity)
Governance_notes:
Not tied to pay so not formally accountable: "The Netflix Board oversees the Company’s ESG efforts, which includes sustainability, with the assistance of the Nominating and Governance Committee. They receive updates on sustainability and enterprise risk management at Board meetings. Executive Management oversees decisions related to climate risk with expert input from internal teams. An annual Company-wide enterprise risk assessment is performed, in which climate risks are considered, and the findings of this assessment are shared with our Board annually. Our sustainability program, which includes our climate strategy, is led by our Netflix Sustainability Officer" (Netflix Environmental Social Governance Report 2024, pg. 40).

"Our independent accountants, EY, have provided limited assurance over our 2020-2023 Scope 1, 2 and 3 greenhouse gas emissions inventories (location- and market-based), and separately assured our retirement of carbon credits" (Netflix Environmental Social Governance Report 2024, pg. 13).
“Climate performance is reviewed annually by the Netflix Board and executive management. The company’s Sustainability Officer oversees implementation of decarbonization initiatives and reporting. Netflix conducts annual third-party assurance of emissions data and carbon credit retirements.”
Carbon_credits_conditions: Must be high environmental integrity|Avoid social harm|Avoid biodiversity harm|Other conditions
Carbon_credits_conditions_other:
"Any credits that we purchase must meet globally recognized core quality criteria and be:
- Additional
- Verified by a 3rd party
- Based on a conservative and realistic baseline
- Not double counted
- Durable
- Issued by a credible standard with robust provisions for reversal risk, and accounts for leakage (the risk of displacing emissions from one location to another)" (Netflix Environmental Social Governance Report 2024, pg. 44).
Removals_and_credits_notes:
“Netflix currently uses high-integrity, third-party verified carbon credits to neutralize residual emissions while continuing to reduce absolute emissions in line with its 2030 target. The company’s portfolio focuses on nature-based removals and emerging CCS technologies, with a long-term plan to replace offsetting with in-boundary carbon removals.”

Nature climate solutions: In 2024, we made investments in reforestation projects that harness advancements in earth observation data. (~70% of carbon credits retired to match remaining emissions in 2024 consisted of nature based projects)

Name: X
Targets_notes:
Twitter does not have any known climate targets after Elon Musk acquired the Company in 2022.

In 2021, the Company adopted Science Based Targets and committed to setting net zero and near term targets ("By adopting Science Based Targets, Twitter will have a maximum of two years to set targets for its Scope 1, 2, and 3 greenhouse gas emissions, without relying on carbon offsets." (https://www.commondreams.org/newswire/2021/04/23/twitter-commits-set-science-based-climate-target)" The Company had since announced some sectoral targets set for parts of the company (e.g. "In 2019, we shared plans to achieve 100% carbon-neutral power sourcing in our current data centers by the end of 2022. [...] Our Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) are sourced from solar and wind power projects in the same geographic region in which energy was used, and cover 100% of Scope 2 emissions from these sites. ", and in 2022 "joined the EU climate pact, committing to ambitious North Star and Pathway pledges, in line with Paris Agreement goals. We’re committed to transitioning to renewable electricity in all our EU leased operations; using 100% carbon-neutral energy in our directly leased buildings by 2025; and upping our investments in carbon removal technologies...By 2030, we’re set to have significantly reduced our greenhouse gas emissions, paving the way for our net-zero journey." https://blog.twitter.com/en_us/topics/company/2022/accelerating-our-climate-commitments-on-earth-day). 

However, Twitter's commitment was removed after the company was acquired by Elon Musk in 2022. There was no further mention of the company's climate commitment after the acquisition. As of today, the SBT website shows the status of Twitter Inc's "Near-term target" and "Net-zero target" both as "Commitment Removed" (https://sciencebasedtargets.org/target-dashboard)
Governance_notes:
The Company's first Global Impact Report launched in 2021 also seemed to be its last: 
Announcement: https://blog.x.com/en_us/topics/company/2021/introducing-twitters-global-impact-report
Report: https://about.twitter.com/content/dam/about-twitter/en/company/global-impact-2020.pdf
Investor Relations Blog (last updated in July 2022): https://blog.twtrinc.com/
Removals_and_credits_notes: The company used carbon offset and investments in carbon removal technologies back in 2019, but after Musk's acquisition, there is no information on whether carbon offset will continue to be used or incorporated into any of its future emission reduction targets, if and when they are to be set.

Name: LendLease
End_target_text: Our Mission Zero goes beyond achieving Net Zero for Scope 1 and 2 emissions. Our industry-leading Absolute Zero by 2040 target aims to eliminate Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions within Lendlease’s defined boundaries and without the use of offsets. (Lendlease Annual Report 2025, p20)
Interim_target_text: We are targeting the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions from business activities as far as possible, with the remainder offset through approved carbon offset schemes. Our Net Zero by 2025 target applies to Scope 1 and 2 emissions.  (Lendlease Annual Report 2025, p20)
Targets_notes: "We have achieved our first milestone target—Net Zero for Scope 1 and 2 emissions—via decarbonisation strategies under our Mission Zero Roadmaps". (Lendlease Annual Report 2025, p20)
Coverage_notes:
Scope 1: Direct emissions from fuels burned in operations, such as petrol, diesel, and gas used in fleet vehicles, cranes, and boilers.
Scope 2: Indirect emissions from purchased or generated electricity for buildings and sites.
Scope 3: Indirect upstream and downstream emissions, including raw material manufacturing, transportation, tenant energy use, and business travel.
(Mission Pathways Webpage: https://web.archive.org/web/20251203120414/https://www.lendlease.com/au/sustainability/climate-and-environment/mission-zero/what-is-mission-zero/)

Lendlease uses tCO2-eq as a unit measurement for Scope 1 to 3. CO2-eq refers to the global warming potential (GWP) of 7 greenhouse gases including: carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, HFCs, PFCs, SF6 and NF3. The CO2-eq unit is the equivalent of one metric tonne of these greenhouse gases in comparison to the impact of one metric tonne of CO2.							
 (Source: Lendlease FY25 ESG Databook, source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251203114335/https://www.lendlease.com/siteassets/lendlease/shared/sustainability/reporting-and-disclosure/esg-databook/lendlease-fy25-esg-databook.xlsx)
Published_plan_measures: Measures for all emission scopes that are covered by the target, Information on the extent to which measures will be applied (e.g. if switching to EVs, what share of the fleet; if installing an own solar PV installation, what is the installed capacity), Schedule for regular review of measures
Governance_notes:
The Board of Directors (Board) is ultimately responsible for Lendlease’s strategic decisions in relation to the management of climate-related risks and opportunities, and has established
two permanent committees to assist in its role: the Risk and Sustainability Committee and the Audit Committee (2025 Annual Report, p26). 

The company does not explicitly state how much executive compensation is affected by delivering on climate goals, but there is an indication of this in the 2025 Annual report (p44, 48, 49), where they disclose that ESG- and climate-related metrics (including progress on its Mission Zero / net zero and absolute zero carbon goals) are incorporated into performance scorecards used to determine variable remuneration outcomes for senior leaders.
Carbon_credits_conditions: Must be high environmental integrity|Not include avoided emissions (e.g. via renewable energy projects)|Not include emissions reductions (e.g. via greater efficiency)

All remaining [no specific figures provided] Scope 1 emissions are compensated primarily through high-quality nature-based offsets within the Australian Carbon Credit Unit scheme.
Offsets are centrally procured through a long-term offtake agreement with Tasman Environmental Markets (TEM), sourced from the Wongamere native regeneration project in Queensland.(Lendlease Annual Report 2025, p20, https://web.archive.org/web/20251203105302/https://www.lendlease.com/siteassets/lendlease/shared/investor-centre/announcements/asx/2025/08/2930419.pdf)
The 2040 target ("Absolute Zero Carbon by 2040") excludes the use of offsets.

Name: S&P Global
End_target_text: Net-zero total GHG emissions by 2040
Interim_target_text: 25.2% reduction in absolute Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions (equivalent to a 25% reduction per square foot)
Targets_notes: The company has set the following climate targets: (1) 2025 Near-Term Science-Based Targets: (1.1) 25.2% reduction in absolute Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions (equivalent to a 25% reduction per square foot), (1.2) 25% reduction in absolute Scope 3 GHG emissions from employee travel, (1.3) 81% of our spend allocated to suppliers who set their own science-based targets. (2) 2030 targets: (2.1) Net-zero Scope 1 and 2 emissions, (2.2) 100% renewable energy use in Scope 2. (3) Net-zero Scope 3 emissions from global operations within leased and sublet location by 2035. (4) Net-zero total GHG emissions by 2040. For more information, refer to the 2024 Impact Report, page 42.
Coverage_notes:
1. Note on Gases Covered: The report does not explicitly specify which greenhouse gases (CO₂, CH₄, N₂O, etc.) are included or excluded under company’s emissions accounting.
2. Note on Previous Emissions: The targets use 2019 as the baseline year, indicating that emissions generated prior to 2019 are not included.
Governance_notes:
1. Note on Public Plan: While the 2024 Impact Report mentions some climate-related measures, there is no indication of a comprehensive, publicly available plan to meet the targets.
2. Note on Public Reporting Mechanism: The company provides regular updates on its progress through its annual Impact Report.
3. Note on Equity: The targets apply only to the company’s own operations.
4. Note on Leadership Accountability: While the reporting indicates that certain sustainability indicators are included in remuneration, it does not clarify whether, or how, specific climate-related targets are embedded in individual or collective leadership objectives or performance evaluations.
Removals_and_credits_notes: As mentioned in the 2024 Impact Report (page 44), in 2024 the company purchased and retired a total of 55,000 certified carbon credits from the Extractivist Reserve (RESEX) Rio Preto-Jacundá REDD+ project in Brazil. The project is a collaboration between Biofílica and local residents, aimed at promoting sustainability in the extractive community by reducing forest degradation and illegal deforestation. Located in a 95,000-hectare reserve in Rondônia, Brazil, the project focuses on community-led initiatives that enhance climate adaptation, support local residents’ management of forest resources and provide benefits for biodiversity, including the protection of threatened species. The carbon credits are accredited by the Verified Carbon Standard. Carbon offsets are not counted as progress toward the targets, so the answers to offset/removal-related questions are "No".

On historical emissions, Google does not include it is the 2030 target because the company claims to have offset it entirely through carbon credits purchase: 'As of today, we have eliminated Google’s entire carbon legacy (covering all our operational emissions before we became carbon neutral in 2007) through the purchase of high-quality carbon offsets. This means that Google's lifetime net carbon footprint is now zero.' (source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260130154121/https://blog.google/company-news/outreach-and-initiatives/sustainability/our-third-decade-climate-action-realizing-carbon-free-future/)

Governance_notes:
The rapid, non-linear growth of AI energy demand and evolving government policies may impact the precision of future emissions forecasting and the ability to hit targets stated in the public plan. Because of these factors, the 2025 Environmental report describes the projected emissions curves leading to 2030 as 'illustrative' (p118, footnote 127). 

The target plan does not explicitly reference “equity” or “just transition,” nor does it address the rights or transition of workers in fossil-fuel-intensive sectors. But, it includes indirect equity-related elements, notably support for vulnerable and underserved communities (e.g. climate resilience tools, flood forecasting in developing regions), partnerships with Indigenous communities on environmental restoration projects, workforce development for clean energy infrastructure (including training and job creation in advanced nuclear), and efforts to democratise access to clean energy and environmental data in the Global South through open tools and funding initiatives (2025 Environmental Report, p12, 26, 65-70). 

Alphabet’s board committees, including the Audit & Compliance Committee, do not have formal, chartered accountability for environmental target delivery. The Compensation Committee introduced an ESG bonus program in 2022 that included environmental performance components for senior executives, but the linkage to specific climate targets or measurable environmental KPIs is qualitative and not clearly defined in public disclosures (Alphabet Notice of 2025 Annual Meeting of Stockholders and Proxy Statement, source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260130154414/https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000130817925000511/goog012701-def14a.htm). Compensation impact related to climate target delivery is therefore limited and discretionary rather than formally mandated.
Removals_and_credits_notes:
Alphabet no longer claims carbon neutrality via offsets. Instead, it invests in durable carbon-removal technologies. The company clearly lists carbon removal projects, their estimated contracted credits and time frames in their 2025 Environmental Report (p106). Google intends to apply these credits in 2030 and release detailed methodology. 

Through Frontier, a USD 200 million coalition (with Stripe, Shopify, and Meta), Google advances early-market support for engineered removals (DACCS, BECCS, mineralization). These are intended for neutralizing residual emissions post-2030.

End_target_text: BHP is committed to achieving net zero operational greenhouse-gas (GHG) emissions (Scopes 1 and 2) by FY2050. The company has also set a medium-term target to reduce operational GHG emissions by at least 30 percent by FY2030, using a FY2020 baseline. This target covers all BHP-operated assets and is supported by a publicly available Climate Transition Action Plan (CTAP 2024 - https://web.archive.org/web/20251005190858/https://www.bhp.com/sustainability/climate-change/climate-transition-action-plan), which details pathways and assumptions for reaching the goal. BHP is also “working towards” net-zero value-chain (Scope 3) emissions by 2050, but this is an ambition rather than a formally validated target.
Interim_target_text: BHP’s medium-term target is to reduce operational (Scopes 1 and 2) GHG emissions by at least 30 % by FY2030 relative to the FY2020 baseline. The pathway relies primarily on structural abatement (e.g. renewable power procurement, energy efficiency, diesel replacement trials, and methane management) rather than voluntary offsets. As of FY2025, BHP reports remaining “on track” for this goal and has already reduced operational emissions by ~32 % from the baseline (Annual Report 2025, Climate Change Section 9.8 and CTAP 2024).
Targets_notes: Medium-term reduction applies to operated assets only. Progress is monitored annually through emissions inventory updates and audited data. Use of voluntary offsets excluded except as a “contingency measure.” Post-2030 path will depend on technological maturity in diesel replacement and methane abatement.

Name: Kimberly-Clark
End_target_text: In 2020, after achieving our 2022 GHG reduction goal early, we announced our current 2030 SBTi-approved goals, to reduce the carbon footprint of our products and brands by reducing our direct and indirect (Scope 1 + 2) emissions by 50% and value chain emissions (Scope 3) for purchased goods & services and end of life treatment of sold product by 20% versus a 2015 base year.
Targets_notes: The targets are aligned with SBTI (scienced-based targets initiative).
Coverage_notes: The target covers all greenhouse gases (GHGs). The Scope 1 and 2 absolute emissions reduction target is 50% from a 2015 base year by 2030. The Scope 3 target is partial, covering a 20% absolute reduction in Categories 1 (Purchased Goods and Services) and 12 (End-of-Life Treatment of Sold Products) from a 2015 base year by 2030. The target does not include neutralizing historical emissions. As of the end of 2024, the company has achieved a 43.3% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions and a 16% reduction in Scope 3 (Categories 1 & 12) against the 2015 baseline.
Published_plan_measures: Measures for all emission scopes that are covered by the target, Information on the emission reductions expected from these measures within a certain time period, Information on the extent to which measures will be applied (e.g. if switching to EVs, what share of the fleet; if installing an own solar PV installation, what is the installed capacity), Schedule for regular review of measures
Governance_notes: For nearly two decades, Kimberly-Clark has published an annual Sustainability Report to provide progress updates on the company’s environmental, social, and governance (ESG) matters.
Removals_and_credits_notes: The 2024 Sustainability Report does not specify the use of carbon credits (offsets) to meet its emissions reduction targets. The report recognizes the role of forests in carbon removal, stating: 'Forests are the world’s best natural mechanism for removing CO2 from the atmosphere, sequestering it in tree mass and soil.' However, it does not state that the company's forest-related initiatives, such as its sustainable sourcing policy or conservation projects, are used as carbon removals within its operational target boundary to neutralize its reported emissions.

Governance_notes:
The monitoring, management, and oversight of climate-related risks and opportunities is a key responsibility of the Board. (FY25 Annual Report, p76) 
Our Climate Change Policy serves as the cornerstone of our commitment to addressing the global challenge of a changing climate, guiding our actions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, enhance resilience, and drive innovation. The Policy defines our approach to integrating climate considerations into decision-making, ensuring alignment with our purpose to accelerate decarbonisation on a global scale, rapidly and profitably. (FY25 Annual Report, p77) 
Two key committees are used to maintain oversight of climate-related activities including progress against our Climate Transition Plan: Executive Sustainability
Committee & Decarbonisation Steering Committee. (FY25 Annual Report, p77-78) 
Targets related to emission reductions have existed in the LTIP (Long-Term Incentive Plan) since FY21. From FY24, targets have also been incorporated into all short-term incentive plans to continue to drive the link between variable remuneration and our decarbonisation activities for all employees across our business. (FY25 Annual Report, p78) (https://web.archive.org/web/20250902145531/https://content.fortescue.com/fortescue17114-fortescueeb60-productionbbdb-8be5/media/project/fortescueportal/shared/documents/regulatory/asx-announcements/2935109-fy25-annual-report-and-appendix-4e.pdf)
Carbon_credits_conditions_other: In 2023, Fortescue ceased purchasing voluntary carbon offsets for Scope 1 and 2 emissions, instead focusing our efforts on the elimination of emissions. Carbon offsets against Scope 1 and 2 emissions are purchased and relinquished only to the extent required by legislation. Our participation in compliance markets is therefore limited to purchases required only to the extent of law, tapering in line with facility-level decarbonisation plans. (FY25 Annual Report, p87)
Removals_and_credits_notes:
Fortescue is committed to genuine decarbonisation and elimination of fossil fuels, without reliance on carbon removals (Fy25 Climate Transition Plan, p31); We prioritise absolute emissions
reductions and do not plan for carbon removal activities in our business operations (Fy25 Climate Transition Plan, p37).

Scope 1 Emissions, Scope 2 Fuel Combustion Emissions, and Scope 3 Business Travel :Emissions We will purchase carbon offsets as needed to achieve carbon neutrality. Scope 2 Electricity Emissions.: Our carbon reduction strategy for Scope 2 emissions will be achieved through reductions in energy consumption and total office space and through purchase of 100% renewable energy through local tariffs, RECS and EACs. Since 2002, Xerox has performed an annual greenhouse gas inventory. Our GHG inventory methodology follows the World Resources Institute Greenhouse Gas Protocol, tracking the six major GHGs and expressing our carbon footprint in terms of carbon dioxide equivalents (CO2e). Our Scope 1 emissions include direct emissions from the combustion of fossil fuels in our facilities, primarily natural gas, and the combustion of gasoline and diesel fuels in our service and sales vehicle fleet. Our Scope 2 indirect emissions included in the inventory primarily result from purchased electricity and steam at our manufacturing sites, offices, warehouses and electric service vehicles. Xerox applies market-based methodology for scope 2 reporting.

Scope 3 emissions result from Xerox activities but occur at a third party and/or arise from sources we do not own or control. emissions reduction goals. We are further advancing our emissions measurement and are proud to release our first-ever

• Change in boundary: We reported all our global businesses and fleet data within our operational control for the
first time.
• Change in methodology: Sites that were previously reported as scope 3 moved to scope 1 and 2.
• Portfolio growth: Through business combinations.
Global operations that are not within UnitedHealth Group’s operational control include joint venture operations in Peru
and in the U.S.

significant categories of scope 3 data in our 2022 Sustainability Report.

Name: Lockheed Martin
End_target_text: Our updated commitment, which received executive-level approval, is to reduce our absolute Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions by 36% from a 2020 baseline. This updated commitment is in line with the absolute contraction model well-below 2°C scenario.
Targets_notes: Updated from previous commitment: Our updated carbon emissions reduction goal represents a shift from intensity-based emissions models to a commitment in absolute terms and from an updated baseline. Lockheed Martin was an early adopter of science-based carbon reduction goals. Our initial 2025 SMP emissions reduction goal aligned with the methodology of the Center for Sustainable Organizations (CSO), one of the first organizations to tie climate science to more tangible corporate goal-setting. At that time we selected an intensity-based goal that was established to outperform the CSO model criteria for aligning with a 1.5°C outcome in the long-term. In updating our performance commitment, we included three transformational elements: a shift to an absolute carbon reduction measurement, an acceleration of the total carbon reduction to which we are committed, and an update of the baseline year from which we measure our performance to make that commitment more current, relevant and challenging.

End_target_text: We have committed to a companywide target of reducing Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions by 40% by 2034, from a 2019 base year. The target was developed using standards articulated by the Greenhouse Gas Protocol and the Science Based Targets Initiative and is aligned with efforts to limit global temperature increase to well below 2 degrees Celsius. In order to achieve this goal, each business unit has its own road map to align with the overall companywide target.
Targets_notes: The 2021 Carbon Reduction Plan states that it presents the company's "roadmap to achieve Net Zero emissions by 2050" (pg 2, https://web.archive.org/web/20241221214057/https://generaldynamics.uk.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/FINAL-GDUK-Carbon-Reduction-Plan.pdf). However, end target text from 2022 specifically states that the target has not been submitted to SBTi, and no other company materials reference a net zero target. Not a member of Business Ambition for 1.5/Science Based Targets.
Coverage_notes: 2022 Corporate Sustainability Report addresses Scope 3 emissions, but target text specifies Scopes 1 and 2. "Because we are a government contractor, many Scope 3 emissions attributable to our company under relevant protocols, both upstream and downstream, are driven by policy choices made by our government customers. (pgs. 32 and 34, https://web.archive.org/web/20240725210939/https://www.gd.com/-/media/gd-corporate/responsibility/gd-2022-corporate-sustainability-report.ashx)

Selection criteria:
• High quality : additional, quantifiable, real, permanent, and with social co-benefits
• Nature-based: includes multiple environmental and/or social co-benefits beyond carbon removal
• Support technological advances: Direct air carbon capture and storage/sequestration can be considered where nature-based solutions are insufficient or limited within the jurisdiction. 
• Socially responsible: Involve transparent and inclusive consultation and partnerships with local communities.
• Newmont Operational Boundaries: Preferentially within company-owned or controlled areas to provide direct management oversight and quality assurance.
• Sustainable: Designed to exist long-term beyond Newmont’s direct involvement and financial support; Safeguarded against deterioration, destruction or leakage.
• Scalable: Present the opportunity for growth and expansion to remove more carbon than initially designed.
• Verifiable and certifiable: Credits can be generated under recognized and respected programs and protocols
• Reportable: Carbon removals are readily measurable, adhere to accounting practices, and enable transparent public reporting.
Removals_and_credits_notes: Newmont focuses mainly on nature-based removal solutions but also plans to use CCS-based methods if nature-based options are not sufficient: "Achieving our carbon-neutral goal by 2050 may require carbon removal methods – often called carbon offsets – to neutralize hard-to-abate residual emissions that cannot be eliminated. These methods may include carbon sequestration or capture, as well as the implementation of nature-based solutions. (...)  We will prioritize offsets that achieve co-benefits for nature enhancements such as investments in nature-based solutions near our operations and legacy sites. While carbon neutralization applies to our 2050 roadmap, it is not currently considered part of our 2030 GHG emissions reduction targets." (Approach to Energy and Climate Change, p.7)

Name: Cheniere Energy
End_target_text:
Cheniere Energy does not outline a company-wide net zero emissions target. Instead, it highlights specific sustainability commitments, such as a voluntary Scope 1 methane emissions intensity target of 0.03% across its two liquefaction facilities by 2027.
source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260115082905/https://cheniere.s3.amazonaws.com/media/2024-CR-Report.pdf
Interim_target_text: 0.03% Scope 1 methane emissions intensity by 2027 (liquefaction facilities only)
Targets_notes:
Cheniere has set a Scope 1 methane emissions intensity reduction target to consistently maintain 0.03% per tonne of LNG produced across its Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi liquefaction facilities by 2027, covering only Scope 1 methane from liquefaction assets, with no quantified Scope 2 or Scope 3 targets, no disclosed baseline year or percentage reduction versus baseline, and positioned as an interim emissions intensity reduction target within its broader climate strategy, which does not specify a firm company-wide net-zero year in the available disclosures.

Company itself does not mention this target in reporting or on website.
INGAA association states "reaching net-zero greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from natural gas transmission and storage by 2050". Nevertheless, Cheniere has no mention of any targets whatsoever. Not in their annual reports, not in their Corporate Responsibility report, and no mention in quarterly reports either as of 2Q 2023. Only 0.30% of total energy as of YE 2022 is renewable energy per own database on Investor Relations.

"We continue working to reduce GHG emissions intensity from our own operations through facility design and the use of advanced technologies to actively monitor emissions at our facilities and along pipelines."
Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20250819111526/https://cheniere.s3.amazonaws.com/media/2022-Corporate-Responsibility-Report.pdf

"Because methane has a much higher global-warming impact than CO2, we are very focused on reducing these emissions."
Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251113023721/https://www.cheniere.com/our-responsibility/climate/managing-emissions-in-our-operations-and-supply-chain
Coverage_notes: Cheniere reports Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions for its operations and uses life cycle assessment and Cargo Emissions Tags to estimate selected value chain (Scope 3) emissions, but its only quantified mitigation target is a Scope 1 methane emissions intensity reduction target for liquefaction assets (0.03% by 2027), with no quantified company-wide Scope 2 or Scope 3 reduction targets disclosed.
Published_plan_measures: Schedule for regular review of measures, Measures for all emission scopes that are covered by the target
Governance_notes: The Board of Directors, mainly through its Governance and Nominating Committee, oversees climate strategy and related risks, while management (including senior executives responsible for corporate development, strategy and public/government affairs) is tasked with implementing climate and emissions initiatives and reports at least annually through the enterprise risk assessment process and regular Board updates; however, while this framework creates formal oversight and executive accountability for climate matters, including the methane emissions intensity target, the company does not clearly link this target to a quantified, company‑wide net‑zero goal or equity considerations in its governance disclosures.
Removals_and_credits_notes: Cheniere does not disclose the use of traded carbon credits to achieve its Scope 1 methane emissions intensity target and has no separate targets for emissions reductions and removals, although it has previously used offsets for specific “carbon-neutral” LNG cargoes with partners and is exploring CCS on its own CO₂ streams (acid gas removal units) as an internal mitigation option rather than as a quantified removals target.

Name: Xilinx
End_target_text:
Xilinx has not published a formal, company-wide net-zero target as a standalone entity, but as a subsidiary of AMD, its operations and goals are integrated into AMD's broader corporate responsibility efforts and sustainability initiatives. AMD's goals: 50% absolute reduction in greenhouse gas emissions from AMD operations (Scope 1 and 2) by 2030 (base year 2020)
 Since 2014, we have publicly pursued a science-based target for AMD operations (Scope 1 and Scope 2 market-based), meaning a goal we believe meets the level of decarbonization
stipulated by the Paris Climate Agreement. Our current goal, a 50% reduction in operational emissions from 2020 to 2030, is aligned to a 1.5-degree scenario and equates to a target
ambition of approximately 4.2% linear annual reduction, as set forth by the Science-based Targets Initiative, though we recognize that progress may not be linear due to variations in
certain years.
From 2020-2024, we have achieved a 28% reduction in operational emissions, despite a 33% increase in operational energy use over the same timeframe. Our progress is primarily
driven by a more than 2x increase in renewable energy sourced from 2020-2024. Planned operational expansions in the second half of this decade will make our 2030 goal challenging
given the corresponding increase in electricity use. Nevertheless, we remain steadfast in working to achieve our 2030 goal. (See Implementation Strategies for Operations.)

Informed by our materiality assessments, scenario analysis, past goals and future projections, AMD sets timebound climate-related goals to address key emissions challenges and
opportunities. In 2025, we are approximately halfway through our ten-year operational goal, while concluding several five-year Scope 3 related goals and setting new Scope 3 related
goals for 2030. The following section describes our progress and insights as we target our priority sources of emissions. Annual updates on our goals are highlighted in our AMD
Corporate Responsibility website and annual Report.

Name: Western Union
Targets_notes:
Based on Wayback Machine, the Western Union's ESG website (https://corporate.westernunion.com/esg/), where they official release investor-relevant information on their ESG metrics, has been down as early as July 2025. The website remains effectively offline until the company fixes it. This shows the company has weak interest in maintaining public accountability to their ESG pledges. Link to the website in mid-2025: https://web.archive.org/web/20250709122550/https://corporate.westernunion.com/esg/

The latest ESG report is their 2023 report, where they disclose environmental performance data, including energy intensity and Scope 1 and 2 emissions, but does not set a net zero target or quantified emissions-reduction goals. Environmental disclosure alone does not constitute a commitment to net zero (p63)
Coverage_notes: There is no climate target.
Governance_notes:
Western Union claims to provide annual public reporting (P71, 2023 ESG Report), but efforts have discontinued since 2023. 

While ESG oversight is clearly institutionalised (P41, 2023 ESG Report), responsibility is spread across multiple bodies, which can dilute accountability. There is no single committee or role explicitly accountable for climate target delivery (e.g. emissions reductions or net-zero milestones), only general ESG oversight. 

Western Union’s executive compensation framework references ESG performance, but the linkage is high-level and qualitative. There is no indication that compensation is materially or quantitatively tied to specific climate or environmental target delivery. The Compensation Committee oversees ESG alignment, and ESG factors may be considered in individual performance modifiers, but a distinct climate KPI affecting pay is not disclosed. The existing ESG connection appears more compliance and reputation oriented than tied to environmental outcomes. (p32, SEC Schedule 14a Western Union Company, Notice of 2024 Annual Meeting of Stockholders, Proxy Statement and 2023 Annual Report, https://web.archive.org/web/20260130161809/https://d18rn0p25nwr6d.cloudfront.net/CIK-0001365135/eea3c647-f16c-478c-b24f-25d3b309c72d.pdf)

There is mention elsewhere that Executive bonuses (for NEOs other than the CEO) are subject to a ±25% modifier, and that this modifier is based on the Compensation Committee’s qualitative assessment of: Leadership, ESG, Customer focus. ESG is therefore one of several factors that can adjust the final bonus payout, and total payouts are capped at 200% of target bonus. Again, there is no climate and emissions-specific metric (Ibid., p42).
Removals_and_credits_notes: There is no climate target and no mention of sinks and credits in their reports.

Climate change update
18 May 2021
Newcrest sets goal of net zero carbon emissions by 2050
Newcrest’s Purpose is “To create a brighter future for people through safe and responsible mining”.
This Purpose underpins our commitment to take on the challenge of climate change and to reduce our greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions.
Our goal is net zero carbon emissions by 2050. Newcrest is taking action to manage climate change risks and opportunities.
In June 2019, we released our Climate Change Policy which outlined our commitment to the sustainable discovery, development and production of gold and copper, together with our plans to identify, assess and report our responses to climate change challenges.
This Policy continues to direct our actions to build a sustainable, resilient business which will thrive in a low carbon future, encompassing:
• a better understanding of the life-cycle GHG emissions for the gold and copper value chains
• increasing the transparency of our climate change reporting of performance metrics and targets
• reporting our energy use, Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions and our performance against targets annually
• working with our suppliers and customers to better understand our Scope 3 emissions
• ensuring that our measuring, reporting and verification processes are robust across all operating sites
• assessing options to increase our use of renewable power and low emission energy technologies
• focusing on opportunities to improve our energy efficiency to reduce energy used and reduce direct mining costs
• identifying and pursuing best practices in the mining and metals industry and partner with technology developers
• assessing climate change scenarios and the projected future price of energy in our medium to long term portfolio
analysis
• partnering with experts and research organisations to identify potential physical threats from climate change at our
current and planned operating sites and invest in appropriate adaptation responses to build resilience
• contributing constructively to policy development in our host countries.

Newcrest now wishes to set a new longer-term goal, which is to achieve net zero carbon emissions by 2050. This goal will apply to our operational (Scope 1 and Scope 2) emissions.
We will also continue working across our value chain to reduce Scope 3 emissions.
We will continue to be guided by our Climate Change Policy as we pursue this.
Our energy and emissions performance is reported in our Sustainability Reports and we support the Taskforce on Climate related Financial Disclosure (TCFD) recommendations for reporting climate change risks and opportunities.

Name: Blackstone
End_target_text: "In 2021, we formalized Blackstone’s Emissions Reduction Program (“ERP”), which includes a target to reduce emissions by 15% on average across certain new investments where we control energy usage during the first three full calendar years of ownership" (P.3, 2024 Sustainability Report). "The 15% Target is not a 15% reduction in Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions for each portfolio company or asset; rather, the target applies on a cohort-by-cohort basis based on the reductions achieved overall by that cohort. " (P.11, 2024 Sustainability Report)
Targets_notes: Blackstone does not have targets set for its own Scope 1 & 2 emissions reductions, but only has this program in place to help manage its Scope 3 financed emission, by supporting companies in their investment portfolio, "cohort" by "cohort", to reduce their S1&S2 emissions.
Governance_notes: "For Blackstone, we calculate our corporate operational GHG emissions for Scope 1, Scope 2 and select Scope 3 categories under the guidance of the GHG Protocol. ", and the Company reports its Scope 1, 2 & 3 GHG emissions in its annual sustainability reports (P.11-12, 2024 Sustainability Report)
End_target_other: supporting companies in their investment portfolio, cohort by cohort, to reduce their overall s1&s2 emissions by 15%

Name: GE Vernova
End_target_text: "GE previously announced an ambition to be a carbon neutral company for its operations by 2030, and net zero for emissions associated with the use of its sold products by 2050. GE Vernova adopts this ambition as our own. A priority for this ambition must be reducing Scope 3 emissions from the use of our sold products, where we have the largest impact, helping to decarbonize power production on a global scale." (P.48, Sustainability Report 2024)
Interim_target_text:
"GE previously announced an ambition to be a carbon neutral company for its operations by 2030...GE Vernova adopts this ambition as our own. " (P.48, Sustainability Report 2024)

On Offset: "While our primary focus is on direct emissions reductions, we plan to balance any remaining emissions with high-quality offsets or removals, supported by internal standards to ensure quality and alignment with our broader sustainability goals....We are also developing an internal quality standard to ensure that the carbon offsets or removals we purchase meet the highest environmental and ethical criteria.
